stages.name: bin_view_154208_204_206_centerline_bracket_repair
stages.reason: On these three frames the lower wiper blade lies with its left hook on top of a chunky BLACK foam/rack holder block on the crate comb-rail. Because blade and block are both black and at the same height, SAM fuses them into one mask whose left end engulfs the block (lower-blade bbox x0=462, with a column-height bulge peaking ~38px over x466-498 versus the ~16px steady blade strip). centerline_trim removes the vertical crate-bar bleed but cannot remove the block, which sits on the blade centerline. A horizontal mask clip (mask_min_x=500) drops the block columns while keeping the blade (steady strip starts at x>=500); the upper blade already starts at x>=509 so it is unaffected. No prompt variant moved the fused left edge, so the clip is the reliable fix. Additionally, on 000206 the lower blade's SAM mask spat a thin ~3-9px-tall horizontal spike off the right tip (x873-892) toward a crate tooth; mask_max_x=872 clips it so the blade ends in a clean rounded tip. The solid blade and both upper-blade tips already end at x<=872, so this max clip does not touch real blade on any of the three frames.

Do not lower mask_min_x (left block returns) or raise mask_max_x (right spike returns); mask_min_x=500 / mask_max_x=872 are specific to the 204-206 camera pose and must not be applied material-wide.
stages.implementation_note: mask_min_x / mask_max_x are post-processing clips added to detect_material_bgr.py (applied to each candidate mask before area/dedup) and wired through run_material_segmentation.py from threshold_overrides.

warning_triangle.label: 三角牌
warning_triangle.actual_visible_object: red emergency warning-triangle storage case (rectangular plastic box with black end caps and printed label), not an unfolded triangle sign
warning_triangle.key_insight: The case is red while every background (green table, gray floor, gray crate, silver bubble wrap) is non-red, so the prompt 'red rectangular object' is the strongest recall signal and false positives are rare. The dominant failure mode is dropping a real case via max_bbox_fill_frac: a perfectly horizontal axis-aligned case fills up to ~0.95 of its bbox, so the fill cap must stay >= 0.97. A too-tight cap silently drops the horizontal case (showing 1 instance where there are 2, or 0 when both are horizontal). Large case+crate merges are bounded by max_area_frac (0.12) and score (the whole-crate mask scores < 0.1), not by the fill cap.

stages.name: discontinuity_repair
stages.reason: 35 frames where the red case mask was incoherent: printed labels / arrows / specular highlights on the case were left as HOLES by the red text-prompt segmentation, so a single solid case came back fragmented. Fix is morphological: binary closing (5x5, 3 iters) bridges thin gaps and binary_fill_holes fills the enclosed label/arrow holes, yielding one solid coherent case mask. Holes here are larger than 1% of the bbox, so the clean_container_fps 1%-cap fill could not remove them — hence a dedicated repair with unconditional fill_holes. fill_holes / mask_close_* are post-process options added to detect_material_bgr.py and wired through run_material_segmentation.py. Each kept mask is then solidified to its per-component convex hull (fill_convex, fill_convex_max_ratio=1.3): this removes the printed-label / arrow / recess concavities that fill_holes cannot reach because they open to the case edge. The 1.3 area-ratio guard skips any component whose hull would add >30% area, so the contact V-pair (20260527_152814__000423: two cases touching at a vertex = one component, hull/area=1.39) is left as the two real cases instead of having the background wedge between the arms filled.
prompts: red rectangular object
red rectangular warning triangle case
red plastic warning triangle storage case
red long rectangular hazard triangle case

stages.name: stick_bar_repair
stages.reason: On these the generic 'red rectangular object' prompt fragmented a long thin case into high-scoring partial blobs (or merged/missed the second case), and those partials out-scored the full-case masks so IoU-dedup kept the partial. Switching to slender-shape prompts ('red stick in tray','vertical red bar','red bar') and DROPPING 'red rectangular object' makes the full single-piece case the top candidate. Verified each frame returns two full coherent cases (residual-red-outside-mask <=0.06). 423 is the contact V-pair whose upper case was entirely missed by the rectangular prompts; 'red bar'/'red stick' recover it. Each kept mask is then solidified to its per-component convex hull (fill_convex, fill_convex_max_ratio=1.3): this removes the printed-label / arrow / recess concavities that fill_holes cannot reach because they open to the case edge. The 1.3 area-ratio guard skips any component whose hull would add >30% area, so the contact V-pair (20260527_152814__000423: two cases touching at a vertex = one component, hull/area=1.39) is left as the two real cases instead of having the background wedge between the arms filled. 20260527_151710__001279 is TWO cases laid end-to-end (collinear, touching at their black end-caps) that look like one long bar; 'red rectangular object' returns a single merged higher-scoring mask (and convex hull then solidified the whole bar into one blob), whereas 'red bar' returns the two cases as DISJOINT masks (IoU=0), so this frame is routed here and excludes 'red rectangular object'. The two cases are separate components, so per-component fill_convex solidifies each without rejoining them.

washer_filler_769.actual_visible_object: white plastic washer-fluid filler tube/neck with a blue funnel-cap. Table views show a single tube next to a large translucent white plastic sheet; bin views show one or two tubes lying among brown cardboard dividers inside a gray crate.
washer_filler_769.key_insight: Two background look-alikes drive the false positives: (1) the large flat translucent WHITE PLASTIC SHEET on the green table matches generic 'white plastic ... tube' prompts and scores as high as or higher than the real tube, so it cannot be removed by score/relative-score — it is bounded by area: the sheet is >=0.08 area_fraction while a real table tube is 0.014-0.024, so max_area_frac=0.05 drops the sheet and keeps the tube; (2) the gray crate rim scores low (~0.4) versus the in-crate tubes (~0.9), so min_relative_score>=0.55 removes it. The generic prompt 'white plastic automotive filler tube' must stay in the TABLE set because it is the only prompt that finds the tube cleanly in 163500 (blue-cap prompts there return only the sheet+tube merged blob, which max_area_frac then drops, leaving an empty frame); it is safe because the sheet it also matches is always oversized. For BIN frames 107/108 the tube lies flat among dividers: the generic prompt fragments it into two divider-bleeding halves, so the bin set EXCLUDES the generic prompt and uses blue-cap/joint prompts that return one coherent (still slightly divider-bleeding) tube mask — this is near the practical limit for text-only segmentation of a thin tube pressed into matching dividers.
